variables.title: Variables
variables.code:
local max_users = 100
local current_user = 'Alice'

-- Variables are global by default if 'local' is omitted
global_var = "Avoid this"

-- Multiple assignment
local x, y = 10, 20

-- Constants (Lua 5.4+ uses <const>)
local MAX_FILE_SIZE <const> = 1024
variables.notes: Always use 'local' to declare variables. Lua 5.4 introduced <const> for local constant variables.

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.code:
local str = "Hello"
local num = 42
local float = 3.14
local bool = true
local nil_val = nil
local func = print
local tbl = {1, 2, 3}

-- Type checking
local t = type(num) -- returns "number"
data_types.notes: Lua has 8 basic types: nil, boolean, number, string, userdata, function, thread, and table.

operators.title: Operators
operators.code:
local a = 10 + 5
local b = 10 ^ 2 -- Exponentiation

-- Equality
local is_equal = (a == 15)

-- Logical operators (and, or, not)
local val = nil_val or "default"

-- Concatenation
local greeting = "Hello" .. " World"
operators.notes: Use '~=' for not equal. The 'or' operator is commonly used for default values.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.code:
local score = 85

if score >= 90 then
    print("A")
elseif score >= 80 then
    print("B")
else
    print("C")
end

-- Ternary alternative (and/or)
local result = (score >= 50) and "Pass" or "Fail"
conditionals.notes: Only 'false' and 'nil' evaluate to false. Everything else, including 0 and empty strings, is true.

for_loop.title: For Loop
for_loop.code:
local items = {'a', 'b', 'c'}

-- Numeric for loop
for i = 1, #items do
    print(items[i])
end

-- Generic for loop (ipairs for arrays)
for index, value in ipairs(items) do
    print(value)
end
for_loop.notes: Lua arrays are 1-indexed. Use 'ipairs' for arrays and 'pairs' for general tables.

while_loop.title: While Loop
while_loop.code:
local count = 0

while count < 5 do
    print(count)
    count = count + 1
end

-- Repeat-until loop
repeat
    count = count - 1
until count == 0
while_loop.notes: Lua does not have 'continue' or '+=' operators. 'repeat...until' evaluates the condition at the end.

functions.title: Functions
functions.code:
local function add(x, y)
    return x + y
end

-- Anonymous functions
local multiply = function(x, y)
    return x * y
end

-- Multiple returns
local function swap(a, b)
    return b, a
end
functions.notes: Functions are first-class values and can return multiple values.

arrays.title: Arrays
arrays.code:
local numbers = {1, 2, 3}
table.insert(numbers, 4) -- Append

-- Arrays are just tables
local len = #numbers

table.remove(numbers, 1) -- Remove first element

-- Sorting
table.sort(numbers)
arrays.notes: Arrays are implemented using tables with contiguous integer keys starting at 1. The '#' operator gets the length.

maps.title: Maps
maps.code:
-- Tables act as maps/dictionaries
local user_roles = {
    alice = "admin",
    bob = "user"
}

user_roles["charlie"] = "guest"

if user_roles.alice then
    print(user_roles.alice)
end

-- Iterate over map
for key, value in pairs(user_roles) do
    print(key, value)
end
maps.notes: Use 'pairs' to iterate over all keys in a table. String keys can be accessed using dot notation.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.code:
local function might_fail()
    error("Something went wrong")
end

-- pcall (protected call) catches errors
local success, err = pcall(might_fail)

if not success then
    print("Caught error: ", err)
end

-- xpcall for custom error handlers
-- xpcall(might_fail, debug.traceback)
error_handling.notes: Use 'pcall' or 'xpcall' to catch errors instead of traditional try-catch blocks.
